title: The Role of the Judiciary in Our Society

topics.title: Justice, Law and the Role of the Judiciary
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; The Connection Between Law and Justice

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the judiciary ensures fair adjudication and keeps laws and executive action within the Constitution.
Define laws as general rules made by the government that carry consequences when they are not followed.
Identify examples of unjust laws in India and elsewhere and explain why they were repealed.

topics.title: Substantive and Procedural Justice
topics.ncert_sections: The Connection Between Law and Justice (aspects of justice)

concepts.learning_objective: Describe substantive justice as concern with whether the final decision is fair, just and reasonable.
Explain procedural justice as a full hearing for every party and the presumption of innocence.

topics.title: The Judicial System and the Supreme Court of India
topics.ncert_sections: The Judicial System in India; The Supreme Court of India

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the unified hierarchy of courts with the Supreme Court at the apex, High Courts and District Courts.
Recall when and under which Article the Supreme Court was established and its role as final interpreter.
State how Supreme Court judges are appointed, their qualifications, strength and retirement age.

topics.title: Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
topics.ncert_sections: Writ Jurisdiction; Public Interest Litigation; Original, Appellate and Advisory Jurisdiction; Special Leave Petitions

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how citizens can enforce Fundamental Rights through writ petitions under Articles 32 and 226.
Explain how Public Interest Litigation lets people raise issues of public concern before the courts.
Distinguish the original, appellate, advisory and special leave jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

topics.title: High Courts, Subordinate Courts and Tribunals
topics.ncert_sections: High Court; Jurisdiction of the High Courts; Subordinate Courts; Tribunals

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the appointment, qualifications, retirement and writ and supervisory powers of High Courts.
Explain the place of subordinate courts in the judicial system and how District Judges are appointed.
Identify specialised tribunals and the categories of disputes each one decides.

topics.title: New Criminal Laws and Digital Technology in the Judicial System
topics.ncert_sections: Digital Technology and Judicial System; Digital Initiatives

concepts.learning_objective: Match the colonial-era criminal laws with the new laws of 2023 that replaced them.
Explain how digital initiatives make the judicial system more accessible and transparent.
Describe arbitration and how a binding award differs from other modes of settlement.
Explain mediation as assisted mutual settlement in which the mediator imposes no decision.
Describe the purpose and legal basis of Lok Adalats and Gram Nyayalayas.
